details:
1. What It Does & How It Works Project Planetary Pulse is an interactive 3D Earth Digital Twin designed to make complex global environmental trends immediately accessible and understandable. Built for the "Be An Earth System Trend Detective!" challenge, the platform combines an autonomous, speed-adjustable rotating 3D globe with a synchronized 2D map view and historical timeline scrubbing.

Users can toggle across multiple interconnected Earth system layers—including Temperature & Temperature Anomalies (ERA5 / NASA GISTEMP), Air Quality Index (AQI), Cyclones & Severe Storms, NDVI Vegetation (MODIS/VIIRS), SMAP Soil Moisture, Canopy Height & Biomass (GEDI Lidar), and SWOT Water Elevation. Clicking any coordinate on the globe opens a localized analytics panel displaying real-time values, historical baseline deviations, global percentile rankings, and a 1-click CSV export option. Additionally, our Scientific Location Comparison tool lets users compare environmental metrics side-by-side between two global cities (such as Mumbai and Sydney).

2. Benefits & Intended Impact Raw satellite and climate datasets are often scattered across technical portals, making it difficult for non-specialists to see how different environmental variables interact over time. Planetary Pulse bridges that gap by turning fragmented numbers into an intuitive visual workspace. It empowers students, educators, researchers, and everyday citizens to spot directional ecological shifts early, compare regional climate impacts, and make informed, data-driven decisions.

3. Tools, Languages & Software Used Frontend & 3D Visualization: React, JavaScript/TypeScript, React Three Fiber (for the interactive 3D Earth globe and rotation speed controls), and Leaflet (for 2D spatial mapping). Data Visualization & UI: Recharts (for time-series trend graphs and baseline deviation charts) and custom responsive CSS. Data Integration & Deployment: Open NASA and partner Earth observation datasets (GISTEMP, MODIS, VIIRS, SMAP, GEDI, SWOT, Copernicus/OpenAQ), version-controlled via Git/GitHub and hosted live on Vercel.

4. Creativity & Key Factors Considered Instead of presenting static graphs or single-variable maps, we focused on interconnectedness and user control. Allowing users to adjust the globe's rotation speed, switch seamlessly between 3D spatial context and 2D analytical precision, and run instant two-city scientific comparisons turns passive data viewing into active exploration. During development, our team prioritized:

Data Clarity: Pairing raw numbers with historical baselines and global percentiles so users immediately understand whether a reading is normal or an extreme anomaly. Performance & Accessibility: Optimizing 3D rendering and layer switching so the web app runs smoothly across devices without requiring specialized GIS software
